Sony Memory Stick Walkman NW-MS7

An early digital music player shaped as a flattened silver capsule, with a translucent blue front and chrome earbuds.

Source
V&A: Sony Memory Stick Walkman NW-MS7, W.665:1 to 14-2001
Creator
Sony Corporation
Made
2000 (V&A)
Style
Y2K aesthetic (agent-proposed, not yet reviewed by a person)
Moods
Futuristic, shiny, techno-optimistic
Evidence
Inspected the V&A photograph of object W.665:1 to 14-2001 (image 2006AF4293, 1271 × 1600) in a scratchpad copy. Not stored.
Reviewed
28 September 2026
Rights
Link and metadata only. License: unverified. Rights policy

Context

The V&A describes a “flattened cylinder form on grey/silver plastic, incorporating a LED display”. The player stored up to 80 minutes of music on a Memory Stick instead of a cassette. V&A W.665-2001.

Observed

  • The body is a long rounded capsule in pale silver plastic. The ends are rounded and the sides curve.
  • A translucent royal-blue panel runs down the front. It narrows in the middle and holds the LCD, the name, and a window for the Memory Stick.
  • “MS WALKMAN” is set in wide, rounded, extended capitals; smaller labels such as “PORTABLE MEMORY STICK PLAYER” are in small spaced capitals.
  • The earbuds are polished chrome with black rims and show sharp highlight lines.

Why it belongs

This is the chrome side of Y2K in a product: silver as the base material, one saturated translucent color, and a wide techno wordmark.

The hourglass-shaped blue panel on the capsule reads like a device interface drawn as an object.

Borrow

Put a translucent color panel on a silver base, and taper it so the base shows at the edges.

Set a short product name in wide rounded capitals, with small spaced capitals as secondary labels.

Use polished chrome with one hard highlight line for small accessories or icons.
